details: Stablecoin liquidity saw a notable drop of $687 million between May 18 and May 24, 2026. Despite this, four public companies collectively added 612 BTC, valued at $47.5 million, to their reserves during the same period. This indicates a potential rotation of capital within the crypto market, with some entities accumulating Bitcoin amidst broader liquidity shifts.
title: Stablecoin Liquidity Declines While Public Companies Increase Bitcoin Holdings

details: The U.S. Senate has made progress in digital asset policy, signaling increasing political support for the crypto sector. Concurrently, Japan is set to recognize foreign-issued stablecoins as legal payment methods starting in June, a move expected to boost cross-border crypto activity and integration.
title: US Senate Advances Digital Asset Policy; Japan Legalizes Foreign Stablecoins

details: A significant whale investor, identified as "nemorino.eth," has acquired 7,908.3 ETH at an average price of $2,113, totaling an investment of $16.71 million in USDC. The acquisition involved an initial purchase, followed by using the acquired ETH as collateral to borrow DAI for further ETH purchases.
title: Whale Investor Acquires $16.71 Million in Ethereum

details: Strive has announced a significant Bitcoin acquisition of $85.4 million, positioning itself ahead of major players like Coinbase and Riot in recent institutional purchases. This indicates strong institutional confidence and continued accumulation of Bitcoin.
title: Strive Purchases $85.4 Million in Bitcoin, Outpacing Competitors

details: The United Kingdom has imposed sanctions on the cryptocurrency exchange HTX due to its alleged involvement in supporting Russian networks. This action is part of a broader sweep by the UK targeting crypto exchanges with ties to illicit activities.
title: UK Sanctions HTX Over Alleged Support for Russian Networks
